opening.client: What is the core problem or opportunity you want to address with this client?
opening.discover:
Sure — let's find you the right template.

**Tell me what you have in mind. You can describe it by what it does ("something that helps clients understand their cash flow"), by a combination of topics ("strategic planning plus team engagement"), or by a name you half-remember ("something like the Working Capital one"). The more detail you give, the better I can match it.**
opening.plan:
Great — let's think through this together.

Before I point you to the right tool, I want to understand where you are and what you're trying to achieve — the best planning framework depends entirely on your situation.

**What's prompting you to think about planning ahead right now?**
opening.learn:
Great — this is one of the most valuable things you can invest in.

To make sure I point you to the right resource, I want to understand what you're looking to develop and what's driving it.

**What area are you most drawn to working on — winning clients, facilitation skills, the psychology side, positioning and messaging, or something else?**
opening.course:
Great — let's design your learning program together.

A good course starts with understanding what you want to develop and why — then we'll shape the right content, pace, and sequence around you.

**What are the skills or advisory concepts you'd like to develop?**

eightLevers.title: 8 Levers
eightLevers.instruction: Move a lever and watch the profit move. The point isn't the numbers — it's which lever pays best. A small lift in margin usually beats a big lift in volume.
eightLevers.marketHint: How many potential customers are in the client's market? Size this to the real business — every scenario below is measured against it.
eightLevers.chainNote: Every customer is won through this chain. Each step multiplies the last — which is why a small gain early compounds all the way to revenue.
eightLevers.compareTitle: Current vs Option B vs Option C
eightLevers.compareNote: The two options from the source model. Look at Option C: it earns LESS revenue than Option B, yet makes MORE profit — because the margin lever outweighs the volume lever. That is the whole lesson.
eightLevers.labourNote: What the business charges per hour against what it actually pays per hour — once leave, sick days and non-chargeable time are taken out. The gap between the target margin and the achieved margin is the point: the labour lines look far more profitable on paper than they are in practice. Move the labour inputs on the left and watch the gap open or close.

coach.heading: What this means
coach.negative: Immediate debts exceed what the business can realise quickly. This is a now conversation: which creditors can wait, what can be turned to cash this week, and what outside support exists.

coach.discountTrap: And note the discount trap: a {d} discount means selling {up} more just to keep the same gross profit.
